issues.description: Parameter name mismatch in Exercise 4 state preparation: the template method signature names the second parameter switch_register, while the problem statement and the rest of the template/solution consistently refer to this register as flip_register. This inconsistent naming in the template (signature vs. docstring/problem text) can confuse students reading the stub (they may wonder whether to use flip_register or switch_register) and slightly harms readability of the starter code. It does not break positional calls, but it is an unintended inconsistency between the problem description and the template.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the parameter in the template state_preparation signature from switch_register to flip_register to match the problem statement and the rest of the code/documentation. Also update any docstring examples to use the same name to avoid confusion.

issues.description: Docstring/parameter mismatch in Exercise 1 simulate() stub: the template simulate method signature accepts only qc (the QuantumCircuit) but its docstring lists both qc and query_register as arguments. This discrepancy between the method signature and its docstring in the template may confuse students about the intended parameters they should implement/expect.
issues.suggested_fix: Update the docstring in the template simulate() stub to reflect the actual signature (only qc) — remove the query_register parameter from the docstring or, if the intended design requires query_register as an argument, modify the method signature accordingly. Keep docstring and signature consistent.

issues.description: In the Lights-Out (Exercise 4) code the same conceptual register is referred to by different names: the problem statement and other functions call it the 'flip' register (flip_register), while the template's state_preparation function signature uses the identifier 'switch_register'. This inconsistent identifier is present within the same template file (docstring mentions flip_register but parameter is switch_register), and the solution uses flip_register. This mismatch creates unnecessary confusion for students mapping the problem text (which repeatedly refers to the 'flip' register) to the template stub they must complete and to the reference solution. Students may be unsure which register to pass to state_preparation or why the docstring and parameter name differ.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the parameter 'switch_register' in the template's state_preparation signature to 'flip_register' (and align the docstring accordingly) so the template, problem text, and solution use the same identifier.
